name: room
text: Room opened — goal: news: Freshness: refresh the AI-news digest from the newest official/company/national sources.

name: Scoop
text: I’ll pull the freshest AI-news from the last 24 h: run `curl -s https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent | grep -oP '(?<=<a href=")[^"]*' | head -n 20 > arXiv-AI-24h.txt` to harvest the latest arXiv AI papers, then `curl -s https://huggingface.co/api/models?sort=updatedAt&direction=-1&limit=20 | jq -r '.[].id' > HF-models-24h.txt` to grab the 20 most-recently-updated Hugging Face models. These two files will land in `/workspace/news-digest/` and serve as the concrete artifact for today’s freshness refresh.

name: Factcheck
text: **Factcheck:** The proposal risks *source bias*—arXiv’s "recent" feed may exclude preprints uploaded outside the 24h window but still cutting-edge, while Hugging Face’s API prioritizes popularity over novelty (e.g., a 2-year-old model with minor updates ranks higher than a fresh breakthrough). Where’s the evidence this captures *true* freshness, not just recency? Demand: cross-validate with at least one national lab or company blog feed (e.g., DeepMind, NVIDIA) to test coverage gaps.
